models_evaluated: convolutional neural network for sperm detection

links.outcome: Embryologist sperm search time and sperm found with versus without AI aid on an ICSI microscope
links.effect: AI-aided embryologist took less time per droplet (98.90±3.19s vs 168.7±7.84s, P<0.0001) and found 1396 sperm vs 1274 without AI, no significant difference in sperm found.
links.quote: In cohort 2, the AI-aided embryologist took significantly less time per droplet (98.90±3.19s vs 168.7±7.84s, P<0.0001) and found 1396 sperm, while 1274 were found without AI, although no significant difference was observed.

links.outcome: AI versus embryologist speed and accuracy identifying sperm in still images on same data
links.effect: AI was faster (0.019±0.30 x 10-5 s vs 36.10±1.18s per field, P<0.0001) and more accurate (91.95±0.81% vs 86.52±1.34%, P<0.001); AI found 611 of 688 sperm vs 560 by embryologist.
links.quote: In cohort 1, the AI model showed improvement in time-taken to identify all sperm per field of view (0.019±0.30 x 10 -5 s versus 36.10±1.18s, P<0.0001) and improved accuracy (91.95±0.81% vs 86.52±1.34%, P<0.001) compared to an embryologist.

screen.reason: The study tests an AI model deployed on a microscope to compare embryologist search performance (time and accuracy) with versus without AI assistance.
